name: Ball Python – Normal (Classic)
short_description: A calm, captive-bred classic ball python hatchling with rich chocolate and gold banding — the ideal first snake.
long_description:
The wild-type ball python is where the hobby started, and it is still one of the most rewarding snakes you can keep. Our normals are hatched here, established on frozen/thawed mice, and handled several times a week so they arrive confident rather than defensive.

## Care summary

- **Scientific name:** *Python regius*
- **Care level:** Beginner
- **Adult size:** 3–5 ft (90–150 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 25–30+ years
- **Diet:** Appropriately sized frozen/thawed mice, then rats, every 7–14 days
- **Temperature:** Warm side 88–92°F (31–33°C), cool side 76–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Humidity:** 55–70%

## Keeper tip

Ball pythons may fast in winter. A healthy adult skipping a few meals is normal — track weight with a gram scale rather than worrying about missed feeds.

name: Ball Python – Pastel
short_description: Bright yellow pastel ball python with clean, lightened sides and greenish blushing — a vivid upgrade on the classic.
long_description:
Pastel is an incomplete-dominant gene that brightens the yellows and cleans up the flanks, giving a sunny look that only improves as the snake matures. It is also one of the most useful building blocks if you ever plan to produce designer combinations.

## Care summary

- **Scientific name:** *Python regius*
- **Care level:** Beginner
- **Adult size:** 3–5 ft (90–150 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 25–30+ years
- **Diet:** Frozen/thawed mice as hatchlings, moving to small rats
- **Temperature:** Basking 88–92°F (31–33°C), ambient 78–80°F (26–27°C)
- **Humidity:** 55–70%

## Keeper tip

Pastels pair well with almost every other gene — a pastel × clown pairing, for example, can produce pastel clowns in the first generation of double hets.

long_description:
Banana (also sold as coral glow) replaces the browns of a normal ball python with soft lavender and warm yellow. Each one picks up its own pattern of small dark speckles as it grows, so no two adults look alike.

## Care summary

- **Scientific name:** *Python regius*
- **Care level:** Beginner
- **Adult size:** 3–5 ft (90–150 cm)

- **Temperature:** Hot spot 90°F (32°C), cool end 78°F (26°C)
- **Humidity:** 55–70%

## Keeper tip

Banana is sex-linked in breeding: banana males often produce mostly male or mostly female banana babies depending on their lineage. Ask us about this animal's line if you plan to breed.
